title: A trace of every agent step, and replay
request: Store a trace for every agent run: one row per step with what the agent saw, the tool and arguments, the verdict, a result summary, tokens and time; show it on the Intern page; and let any finished run be replayed with a scripted model to check it gives the same moves. Never store cell values.
spec: An agent_step table through an Alembic migration (run id, step number, state summary, tool, arguments, verdict, result summary, tokens, seconds); the runtime writes a row per step; replay(run_id) feeds the stored replies back through the runtime with a scripted gateway and checks the same moves result; the trace on the Intern page beside the step list. Done when any finished run can be replayed from its trace with a scripted model and gives the same moves.
plan: Read the storage models, migrations and the intern's step list.
Write the trace store (agents/traces.py) as a new module while A2.2's gate ran, so nothing under test changed; then give run() reply numbers and an optional tracer, both backwards compatible.

Write replay(): the stored replies go through run() again, with the tools answering from the trace, so no model and no project are touched; continue across a run's stops (a question, then a follow-up).
Add the agent_step table (migration 0005) or agent_steps.jsonl; have the intern's own loop write rows until A2.4 moves it onto run().
Return the trace with the session and show each step's trace line on the Intern page; check the API with curl when the built-in browser refused the local page.
Run check-all and the review; fix six findings with tests; commit.

decisions.decision: Replay answers tool calls from the trace instead of running the tools.
decisions.why: Replay checks the agent's decisions, not the tools; running tools would need the original project and could change it.

decisions.decision: A run whose arguments were cut is refused by replay rather than reported as diverging.
decisions.why: A cut argument can never match the original call; reporting it as a different move would be a false regression.

decisions.decision: Result summaries drop the keys that carry table cells (column examples, previews) before the 360-character cut.
decisions.why: The trace is the training source for A6; truncation alone kept the first values of the table.

change: dclab_rnd/agents/traces.py (Tracer, FileTraces, PgTraces, replay); run() stamps each step with its reply number and calls the tracer; migration 0005 adds agent_step; the intern loop writes rows; the server returns the trace with the session and deletes it with the session; the Intern page shows verdict, graph state, model reply and tokens per step; tests/test_agents_traces.py.

findings.defect: Cell values were stored in the trace.
findings.scenario: The standard plan on 'Predict telco churn': trace rows for use_sample and describe_data stored the first customer ids of the table under columns[].examples, in agent_step.result and in agent_steps.jsonl.
findings.cause: The result summary was the first 360 characters of the raw result as JSON.
findings.fix: summary() removes the value-bearing keys (examples, preview and similar) before dumping.
findings.test: A test that runs the data tools and finds none of the table's values in any trace row.
findings.impact: Every standard-plan run on a real table would have written the first customer ids into agent_step and agent_steps.jsonl, which A6 exports for training: the package's one hard rule broken on its first run.
alternatives: Keep only scalar top-level fields of a result, the reviewer's other option: set aside because it also drops structured results (column names, stage statuses) that make a step readable on the Intern page.

findings.defect: The state recorded was after the move, not what the agent saw.
findings.scenario: In the standard plan the create_project row showed a state with a project, though the intern saw none; the use_sample row showed data attached, though the agent saw none. A6.1 needs the state before the move.
findings.cause: The tracer read the graph state when it wrote the row, after the tool ran.
findings.fix: A snapshot is taken before the call and used for the row.
findings.test: A trace test comparing each row's state with the state before its move.
findings.impact: A6.1's records would pair each move with the state after it (create_project shown with a project already there), so a policy trained on them would learn moves for states it never saw at decision time.

findings.defect: Trace step numbers drifted from the session's step numbers, and the page matched on them.
findings.scenario: A session with 8 steps from before the package gets a follow-up: the session's step is 9 but the trace row is 1, so its trace line appears on step 1. Also, a reply [write_plan, get_graph] where get_graph raises reloads the session without the unsaved write_plan, while its trace row stays.
findings.cause: Resuming numbered from the largest stored trace step, not from the session.
findings.fix: The session's own step number is passed to the tracer.
findings.test: A follow-up test where trace and session numbers match.
findings.impact: On a resumed or follow-up session the Intern page showed a step's trace under another step, so a person checking why the agent made a move would read the verdict and tokens of a different call.
alternatives: Resume numbering from the larger of the stored trace number and the session's step count: set aside because it still drifts when a step is reloaded away after an error, while passing the session's own number is exact.

findings.defect: Replay failed on any call made under a legacy alias.
findings.scenario: The model calls set_contract (an old name of set_solution): recorded ok, replayed error, same=False.
findings.cause: The row stored the name as called; the replay stub compared it with the canonical name.
findings.fix: Replay resolves both names through the registry before comparing.
findings.test: A replay test with an aliased call.
findings.impact: Any run where the model used an old tool name would be reported as diverging on replay, a false regression in the check meant to show that an agent's decisions are reproducible.

findings.defect: Replay failed on any call whose arguments had been cut.
findings.scenario: A set_solution call with a long prediction moment and several forbidden columns with reasons: arguments over 1,200 characters were stored as {'_truncated': ...}, which the schema check refused on replay.
findings.cause: A low cut for arguments that are names and sentences.
findings.fix: Arguments are kept up to 8,000 characters; a run with a cut argument is refused by replay with 'arguments were cut'.
findings.test: A replay test with a cut argument.
findings.impact: The runs with long solutions, exactly those that state a detailed prediction moment and forbidden columns with reasons, could not be replayed, so the replay check failed on the runs that matter most.
findings.open: A run whose arguments were still cut (over 8,000 characters) cannot be replayed; it is refused with a reason rather than checked.

findings.defect: The file trace store was fragile, and a trace failure broke the session routes.
findings.scenario: A torn last line left by a crash made delete() raise JSONDecodeError, so DELETE /api/intern/sessions/{id} returned 500 after the session was deleted and left its rows; the next appended row merged into the torn line and was lost; steps() read without the lock while delete() rewrote the file in place; a bad file broke GET of the session.
findings.cause: No handling of bad lines, unlocked reads and in-place rewrites.
findings.fix: delete() skips bad lines and writes a temporary file that replaces the old one; reads take the lock; a record starts a new line when the file does not end with one; the server wraps trace reads and deletes.
findings.test: test_a_broken_store_never_stops_the_run and file-store tests with a torn line.
findings.impact: One crash during an append would make deleting a session return 500 after the session was gone, leave its trace rows behind, lose the next row written, and break opening the session page.

outcome: Done: a row per step in agent_step or agent_steps.jsonl, state taken before the move, no table values in results, replay through run() continuing across stops, and a trace line per step on the Intern page. Open: the tokens of a reply that makes no step are in the session's usage but not the trace; intern traces become replayable when the intern runs on run() (A2.4). The gate passed with 449 tests and the four flows; six review findings fixed.
lessons: A 'summary' made by truncating raw output still carries the first values; remove the value-bearing keys before cutting.
Record the state an agent saw before its move, or the trace cannot teach what to do in that state.
An append-only file needs a plan for a torn last line before anything rewrites it.
risks: A result summary made by truncating raw output keeps the first values of the table, storing cell values in the future training source.
Recording the graph state after the move, which pairs each move with a state the agent never saw.
Trace step numbers drifting from the session's step numbers when a session resumes.
Replay reporting false divergences for aliased names or cut arguments.
An append-only file store that a crash leaves with a torn line, breaking the session routes.
